Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
cartman wrote:
> Nothing is bugging me here, but if a rule states that A cannot perform any D
> action and a card on her states on the contrary that she can actually do it,
> it's not so obvious.
>

> So my Gargoyle can enter combat as the card states :-)

Your Gargoyle has another action option, yes.
He could bleed (a cardless action option open to all minions), hunt (a cardless
action option open to all vampires), diablerize a vampire in torpor, or enter
combat.

And he also cannot perform any directed action.
Which means he can't bleed, diablerize someone else's vampire, or enter
combat with someone else's minion.

"reyda" <true_...@hotmail.com> wrote in message news:<3ea51c4e$0$1076$79c1...@nan-newsreader-02.noos.net>...

What I see here is not something that is bugging him, but an instance
where the rules loop in upon itself. Current rules state that Rule
Text governs game play until Card Text overrides it. The above is
just an example of this... Rule Text alludes that only untapped
minions can take actions (6.2) and actually states that untapped
minions are able to take any actions (6.2.1). This rule is
disregarded with Force of Will text which states Only Usable By A
Tapped Vampire.

>
> you want to know how the line is drawn between rules and card text when one
> should override the other ? Just read the card, plain logic applies. That's
> all.
>

But logic in the case of Kindred Spirits does not work. Which is why
the Prince of Washington DC stated that there should be some Errata on
this. The rules state that By default, your minions bleed actions can
be directed only at your prey. Some cards or effects may allow or
force you to bleed Methuselah other than your prey. You can never
bleed yourself, however. (6.1.1) But the text of Kindred Spirits
state Bleed Any Methuselah. This could override the Rules text.

> for the purpose of the Kindred Spirits stuff, i think that the card which
> says bleed any methuselah prohibits you bleed yourself because the rulebook
> says you may never bleed yourself. It's like entering combat with your own
> vampire, it's also prohibited because the game mechanics don't allow it.

I disagree. The rules has this built into the game as part of its
mechanics. Here I see mechanics opposing each other. It either works
all the time or it doesn't work at all. It it works all the time,
then the game continues with only a minor tweek required (errata
maybe?). If it does not work at all, the game will come to a grinding
halt as card text no longer overrides rules text.
I am all for the minor tweek and a continuation of play.

Michael Eichler
Prince of Spangdahlem

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Ramsteiner wrote:
> But logic in the case of Kindred Spirits does not work. Which is why
> the Prince of Washington DC stated that there should be some Errata on
> this. The rules state that By default, your minions bleed actions can
> be directed only at your prey. Some cards or effects may allow or
> force you to bleed Methuselah other than your prey. You can never
> bleed yourself, however. (6.1.1) But the text of Kindred Spirits
> state Bleed Any Methuselah. This could override the Rules text.

It does. It overrides the default. It allows you to direct the bleed
at Methuselahs who are not your prey, but who are otherwise legal
targets for the bleed.

It doesn't overcome any prohibition against bleeding certain targets,
however. So a Minor Boonee could still not use Kindred Spirits to
bleed his benefactor, since he is not allowed to bleed his benefactor
and card text on Kindred Spirits doesn't have any text to override
that. And he cannot bleed his controller, since he is not allowed to
bleed his controller and card text on Kindred Spirits doesn't have
any text to override that.



> bleed his benefactor, since he is not allowed to bleed his benefactor
> and card text on Kindred Spirits doesn't have any text to override
> that. And he cannot bleed his controller, since he is not allowed to
> bleed his controller and card text on Kindred Spirits doesn't have
> any text to override that.

The impression I'm getting here is that prohibitions are "stronger"
than any permission that doesn't explicitly and specifically say
it's breaking that prohibition. That is, since the rules say you
can't bleed yourself, a card would have to say "you can bleed
yourself" to override that; to overcome the Slave no-D-action
restriction, a card would have to say "even if this vampire is a
Slave" or something along those lines.

Kindred Spirits doesn't *say* that the only prohibition it's
lifting is the "bleeds target your prey" restriction, but since
it also doesn't say that it's making *all* Methuselahs into
legal targets, it doesn't beat other "can't target me" effects
or rules. Is that right?

Josh

questioning legality

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <b83m2d$5ucvf$1...@ID-121616.news.dfncis.de>, Joshua Duffin

<jtdu...@yahoo.com> writes:
>The impression I'm getting here is that prohibitions are "stronger"
>than any permission that doesn't explicitly and specifically say
>it's breaking that prohibition.

Basically, yes.

Consider Absolution of the Diabolist. (Removed from the current
exchanges.)

"This card is playable during your minion phase."

This breaks [1.6.2.3]: "You may play an out-of-turn master card whenever
appropriate during another player's turn. "

However, it doesn't break another bit of [1.6.2.3]: "You may not play a
second out-of-turn card against the same master phase - you'll have to
wait until you square away the debt you owe on the first one."

It simply gives you more /options/ on when to play it. The text "This
card is playable..." doesn't mean you get to break the normal rules
against one card's debt per master phase - though you could argue "But
it says it's playable now, so that over-rides the rules, doesn't it?"

Also, specifically regarding Kindred Spirits. It is arguable that it
doesn't actually over-ride the rules. [6.1.1] notes:

"Some cards or effects may allow or force you to bleed a

Methuselah other than your prey. You can never bleed yourself,
however."

and it is arguable that Kindred Spirits is simply operating within that
statement - some cards let you bleed other Methuselahs. It's one of
them.

This was dealt with some time back, and rewritten in the current rules:

[1.6.3]

"If the ally gains life in excess of his capacity, it doesn’t
drain off, and if the effect inflicts aggravated damage on the
ally, he burns life as normal. However, if the effect would send
the ally to torpor, then he is burned instead."

I believe the ruling you're thinking of was an attempt to resolve the
issue with the rules *as they stood then*. (I recall pointing out one
of the inconsistencies with the situation which resulted in a difficult
ruling - but the only one that made sense with the rules at the time.)

The new rules now stop the bizarre "Shadow Court Satyr in torpor"
situations.

If that's not what you're thinking of, let us know.
